newsitem.title: FRANCE: European states keep FLA plane hopes flying.
newsitem.headline: European states keep FLA plane hopes flying.

text.p: Five European governments on Tuesday kept industry hopes alive of building a new military transporter plane, the Future Large Aircraft (FLA), despite German industry sceptism.

The FLA project, which has been hit by defence budget cuts in France and Germany, is planned as a replacement for ageing Hercules C130 and Transall military airlift planes in eight European countries.
"The following nations, having a common requirement for a military transport aircraft, seek to realise this requirement within a European industrial framework.

"France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Turkey are now ready to officially release a request for proposal to Airbus Industrie, Alenia and Turkish Aerospace Industry," the FLA policy group said in a statement after meeting at the air show.
The British government will look at taking part in the programme this summer, the statement said.
The policy group consists of procurement heads of the FLA programme in Belgium, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain and Turkey, a French procurement official said.

The previous conservative British administration bought 25 Hercules C130J planes from U.S. Lockheed Martin and left an option to buy a further 25 FLAs if the aircraft could be built under commercial conditions.

"Industry has been asked to take immediately the necessary steps to start the pre-launch activities for the Future Large Aircraft and to prepare to establish the industrial organisation," the statement said.
State-owned Aerospatiale of France, Italy's Alenia, British Aerospace Plc and Daimler-Benz Aerospace hope to build the FLA.

But Dasa chief executive Manfred Bischoff told reporters at the air show on Sunday, that a look at the eight countries involved in the FLA and the state of their budgets would show there were other priorities.

The aerospace companies have formed an Airbus Industrie subsidiary, Airbus Military Company (AMC), to run the project on commercial lines. Alenia, part of Italy's Finmeccanica group is an equity partner in AMC.
The programme envisages building 300 FLAs, of which 50 would be for France.
